newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Feb 18.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Local authorities are placed on full alert following growing tension betwen Burmese troops and Karen rebels opposite Ban Duang Dee in Tha Sae district. Residents living along the border will be moved to safety in case of an incursion and the Chong Kha Mew pass, which serves as the trade channel, has been closed. Border police and the army have been mobilised and arms and reinforcements have been deployed to maintain peace in the area. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Constitution Drafting Committee has taken a big step forward by endorsing a proposal that senators must be elected instead of appointed by the prime minister as at present. Panel chairman Anand Panyarachun has stressed that senators have to be recruited via channels that are acceptable to the people and in compliance with democratic principles. The prime minister must no longer be given the sole authority to select senators.

- An 18-wheel trailer truck and a truck carrying dozens of students on a rain-soaked road in northeastern district collided yesterday, killing 11 children and seriously injuring more than 20 others. Eight children died on the spot while three others died in hospital. (THE NATION)

- The government has moved swiftly to set up a working team which will prepare economic and financial data for presentation to Moody's Investors Service analysts when they visit Thailand on March 6 and 7. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Finance Amnuay Viravan has called a meeting of top officials from various agencies and instructed them to collect and prepare the economic and financial data. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh is spearheading a major overhaul of the tourism industry under a seven-point programme agreed between the government and private operators. He has pledged every effort to improve the industry's declining rate of growth as foreign exchange earnings can reduce the country's burgeoning current account deficit. (BANGKOK POST)

- Thailand committed itself to opening all communications services to full competition from 2006 at historic World Trade Organisation telecom talks concluded on Saturday. It is the first time Thailand has clearly specified a timetable for opening its domestic market to foeign competition. (THE NATION)
